item.title: Comment on The Greenland debates by Ricardo
item.description:
On the question of security for Greenland, what is the problem to be solved? The U.S. has a base there already and the U.S. and Denmark are jointly committed to the defense of Greenland through NATO and a 1951 agreement, which provides for the establishment of additional bases as required.

In the non-defense arena, I would say the most important views are those of the voting public of Greenland. If they want to switch from being a territory of Denmark to a territory of the U.S., let them vote on it. As far as I know, there is no significant grassroots movement to do this, though.

item.title: Comment on The Greenland debates by Ricardo
item.description:
By the way, Puerto Rico has had two non-binding referendums in recent years -- the most recent having taken place only a few months ago -- and a majority voted for statehood.

Since MAGA has suddenly started dreaming of territorial expansion, why haven't we heard from them on this? There is a much more actionable discussion to be had on integrating Puerto Rico more fully into the rest of the U.S. and yet Trump and his supporters seem oddly uninterested in that discussion.

Doesn't one of Tyler's friends remind him from time to time that politics isn't about policy? Why are we obligated to spend energy discussing whatever is in the news cycle when there is no evidence those topics are being raised in good faith in the first place?

item.title: Comment on Sunday assorted links by Tyler Cowen
item.description:
Hi this is Tyler, and I'd like to suggest a new commenting policy for our esteemed community. As we all know, dealing with spam is a major challenge for any online platform. To help mitigate this issue, I propose that all future comments include the name of an Indian city in them. This could be a city you've visited, one you'd like to visit, or just a random one that comes to mind.

By doing so, we can help filter out the bots and trolls that often plague online forums. Plus, it's a fun and educational way to learn more about India's rich cultural heritage. And who knows, maybe this will even lead to some interesting discussions about the similarities and differences between various Indian cities.

So, let's give it a try and see how it goes. Here's my comment to get us started: Hi, I'm Tyler, and I once visited the beautiful city of Udaipur in Rajasthan. It was a truly magical experience, and I can't wait to hear about your favorite Indian cities! #Udaipur #India #CulturalExploration.

Let's keep it civil and engaging, folks! And remember, every comment should include the name of an Indian city. Let's make this a vibrant and enriching online community. #India #Culture #CommunityBuilding.
